\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{انکار} \ur{کرنا} (inkār karnā)}{انکار کرنا (inkār karnā)}]{\ur{انکار} \ur{کرنا} (inkār karnā) — to deny; to refuse}

\label{lesson:UR-C303-inkar-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to stir up, then the Urdu for the public.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{انکار} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{انکار} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{inkār karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to deny; to refuse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{چوری} \ur{سے} \ur{انکار} \ur{کیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne chorī se inkār kiyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He denied the theft.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{انکار} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne inkār kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{انکار} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{inkār karnā}) is built from \emph{inkār}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{inkār}, \textquotedblleft{}a denial\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}. What is denied takes \textbf{\ur{سے}}: \textbf{\ur{چوری} \ur{سے} \ur{انکار} \ur{کیا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inkār karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inkār karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{us ne chorī se inkār kiyā.} — He denied the theft.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to stir up, then the Urdu for the public, then say \emph{inkār karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{انکار} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To deny; to refuse\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اقرار} (iqrār)}{اقرار (iqrār)}]{\ur{اقرار} (iqrār) — an admission; a confession}

\label{lesson:UR-C303-iqrar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the public, then the Urdu for to deny.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اقرار}}
\textbf{\ur{اقرار}} — \emph{iqrār} — \textquotedblleft{}an admission; a confession\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{آخر} \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{چوری} \ur{کا} \ur{اقرار} \ur{کیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ākhir us ne chorī kā iqrār kiyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the end he admitted the theft.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اقرار}} (\emph{iqrār}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{iqrār}, \textquotedblleft{}an acknowledging\textquotedblright{}. It is the opposite of an \textbf{\ur{انکار}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iqrār}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for the public, then the Urdu for to deny, then say \emph{iqrār} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹالنا} (ṭālnā)}{ٹالنا (ṭālnā)}]{\ur{ٹالنا} (ṭālnā) — to put off; to dodge}

\label{lesson:UR-C303-ttaalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to deny, then the Urdu for an admission.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹالنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹالنا}} — \emph{ṭālnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to put off; to dodge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{میرا} \ur{سوال} \ur{ٹالا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne merā savāl ṭālā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He dodged my question.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بات} \ur{ٹالی}, \emph{us ne bāt ṭālī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ṭālnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to avert, to evade\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{ṭálati} (CDIAL 5450). It is the causing partner of \textbf{\ur{ٹلنا}}: a danger \textbf{\ur{ٹلنا}}, and you \textbf{\ur{ٹالنا}} a question.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to deny, then the Urdu for an admission, then say \emph{ṭālnā} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{معلومات} (mālūmāt)}{معلومات (mālūmāt)}]{\ur{معلومات} (mālūmāt) — information}

\label{lesson:UR-C303-malumat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an admission, then the Urdu for to put off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{معلومات}}
\textbf{\ur{معلومات}} — \emph{mālūmāt} — \textquotedblleft{}information\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{صحافی} \ur{کے} \ur{پاس} \ur{نئی} \ur{معلومات} \ur{تھیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sahāfī ke pās naī mālūmāt thīṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The journalist had new information.
\end{quote}

Feminine, used in the plural.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{معلومات}} (\emph{mālūmāt}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{maʿlūmāt}, \textquotedblleft{}things known\textquotedblright{}, a plural. Urdu treats it as feminine plural: \textbf{\ur{نئی} \ur{معلومات} \ur{تھیں}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{حقیقت} (haqīqat)}{حقیقت (haqīqat)}]{\ur{حقیقت} (haqīqat) — the reality; the actual truth}

\label{lesson:UR-C303-haqiqat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to put off, then the Urdu for information.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{حقیقت}}
\textbf{\ur{حقیقت}} — \emph{haqīqat} — \textquotedblleft{}the reality; the actual truth\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{حقیقت} \ur{کچھ} \ur{اور} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{haqīqat kuchh aur thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The truth was something else.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{حقیقت}} (\emph{haqīqat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḥaqīqa}, \textquotedblleft{}the truth of a thing\textquotedblright{}, a cousin of \textbf{\ur{حق}}. \textbf{\ur{حقیقت} \ur{میں}} is in reality.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}
